most_serious_defect_in_this_pr: The user_location cleanup is scoped to a single location id while session.remove(location) cascades the DELETE to every descendant location (Location.childLocations is @OneToMany(cascade = ALL, orphanRemoval = true)), so the operation this PR exists to fix still aborts: purging a parent department whose leaf child is assigned to a user throws a referential-integrity violation on user_location(location_id), reproduced at the head sha with a clean positive control. That is the ticket's own expected topology - 'Leaf locations only ... user_location stores the resolved leaf rows' are what get assigned, and a parent department is what an admin deletes. What makes it the most serious rather than merely the most concrete is the second half: the single new regression test provably cannot fail (deleting the cleanup leaves LocationServiceTest#purgeLocation* 4/4 green, because the test never flushes and its assertion is a session lookup that returns null for a session-removed entity), so neither this gap nor the related in-session TransientPropertyValueException is visible to CI, and any future edit that drops or reorders the cleanup ships green as well. The narrow fix is to run the delete over the location's descendants - the same class already has a recursive-CTE getDescendantIds - or to remove the location from the loaded User collections in HQL; either way the test needs a flush+clear+reload (or a direct assertion on the join rows) before it guards anything.
notes: Every one of the 20 came out REAL, which I am flagging rather than hiding: I did not take that on trust. Each mutation claim was re-run independently and reproduced the stated result (drop the native delete -> LocationServiceTest#purgeLocation* still 4/4 green; drop the re-read -> the five new tests still green; drop @Independent -> retireUser retires the assigned locations while 244 tests in the closest suites stay green; add @BatchSize -> 3 collection statements collapse to 1), and every 'this breaks' claim was reproduced at the pristine head sha with a positive control that passes. All 20 anchors are accurate as well: every file:line lands on a line this diff adds and says what the finding says it says, so anchor_wrong is false throughout. The two weakest items, kept REAL but worth knowing: F09 (the LOCATION_ID constant serving both a JPA attribute name and a native-query parameter) is accurate but is nearly NOISE - acting on it changes two lines of naming; and F15 carries one clause I could not support, that the detached-getter hazard is a landmine 'for the companion REST resource' - webservices.rest#762's UserResource3_0 renders the collection off a User it loads in-request (attached) and its search handler routes through getAllowedLocations, which re-reads, so the live landmine is Context.getAuthenticatedUser().getLocations() in module code, exactly as its twin F12 states it. Duplicate grouping is heavier than it looks: 16 of 20 keys collapse into 8 defects, and F10 deliberately appears in two groups because it merges the cascade gap (= F07) and the session-cache caveat (= F05) into one blocking finding. The five singletons are F01 (no @BatchSize), F06 (purge silently un-restricts a user and logs nothing), F09, F13 (advisory-only vs 'allowed to use') and F18 (no add/remove mutators, setLocations(null) breaks the empty-set contract); F01 and F16 are both performance but on different code paths with different fixes, and F06 and F13 are both javadoc asks but about different contracts, so I kept those apart rather than merging them. One disposition is too mild for what the finding itself proves: F08 files the privilege hole as a suggestion where its twin F20 correctly calls it blocking. Things I checked that neither reviewer raised: envers - User is @Audited and the new collection carries no @NotAudited, but no *_audit table exists anywhere in liquibase and Location.tags is the identical audited @ManyToMany, so this matches precedent and is not a defect; purgeUser on a user with assigned locations succeeds, because Hibernate deletes the rows of the collection it owns, so the symmetric FK case is fine; and the changeset's composite primary key diverges from the ticket's proposed surrogate user_location_id, which is harmless but unremarked. Not measured: F19's parenthetical that the entire api suite stays green with the fix removed (I ran only the purge tests; no other test both writes user_location and purges a location, so it is a safe inference rather than a measurement). Worktree left clean at b7cd909d24 - probe classes deleted, all mutations reverted, git status --porcelain empty, and the PR's own new tests re-confirmed green (4/4 purge, 5/5 getAllowedLocations).
